summary: @servicetitan/examples ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: Package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime binary for the detected platform from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable (chmod 0o755), and then invokes it against a 727KB bundled file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style rotated string array `n7gIxM`, rotation function `WV8StW` performing repeated `push(shift())`, `_0x...` renamed identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) and is not the package's advertised content. Bun is fetched specifically to execute this opaque sibling payload outside Node's visibility, giving attacker-controlled bytes an execution channel on the installer's host at install time. The package is published under the `@servicetitan/examples` name with an empty description, no README, and no author/homepage/repository metadata, inconsistent with a legitimate ServiceTitan release and consistent with scope impersonation or scope compromise.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
